chunks: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-'Alawi, from al-'Umarki al-Khurasani, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about fasting three days during hajj and the seven: should he fast them consecutively, or separate them? He said: He fasts the three days without separating between them, and the seven without separating between them, and he does not combine the seven and the three all together.

So this does not contradict the first narration, because his statement عليه السلام, 'he does not separate between the three,' is what is acted upon, since we have already stated that they are to be fasted consecutively. And his statement, 'and the seven, he does not separate between them,' is upon the basis of recommendation and desirability. And his statement, 'and he does not combine the three and the seven all together,' the explanation of it is that fasting the three days is required in hajj, and seven when he returns to his family, so how could he combine them both? But as for the one who missed the three days in hajj until he returned to his family, it is permissible for him to combine them with the seven, as we have already mentioned.

key_terms.السَّبْعَةَ: the seven days of fasting observed after returning
key_terms.الْحَجِّ: the pilgrimage during which the first set of fasting days is observed
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ: the three required days of fasting during hajj
key_terms.صَوْمِ: fasting in the legal context discussed here
key_terms.لَازِمٌ: required or obligatory in this context
key_terms.مُتَوَالِيَةً: consecutively, one after another without interruption
key_terms.يُفَرِّقُ: to separate or space out the fasting days

ai.seo_question: Should the three days of fasting in hajj and the seven days afterward be fasted consecutively or separately?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of fasting the three days in hajj and the seven days thereafter. It indicates that the three days are to be fasted consecutively, while the seven are also mentioned without separation, though this is understood here as recommendation; the three and seven are not ordinarily combined unless the three days were missed until after returning home.
